description: A short tour of the tutorial's three labeled blocks. You read the image datestamp, prove from inside the container that /workspace is your repository, and read the datestamp again after a refresh.
name: walkthrough

steps.description: The image carries a datestamp in the CS374_IMAGE_VERSION variable. This command prints it at the container prompt, so you can read which build you are running.
echo prints the value of the variable. When the course refreshes the container mid-semester, this value changes and tells you a new copy is available.
You are inside the container as the non-root user student, in /workspace. This command proves that /workspace is your cs374-work repository.
ls -la lists every entry in the current directory with its permissions, owner, size and date.

steps.question: The listing shows one file besides the . and .. directory entries. What is it?

steps.description: The . entry is the directory itself and .. is its parent. Everything else in the listing is a file in your repository.
After you check the tool versions, you print the image datestamp one more time.
This is the same datestamp command as the first block. Run it after a refresh to confirm the new image is in place.
The variable expands to the build's datestamp. A value you do not recognize means your copy predates the current image.

title: The CS374 course development environment
